reading.body:
Minnesota's 2025-2026 legislative record shows a coordinated push to constrain data center growth through tax exemption repeals, a proposed moratorium, and new water and environmental review requirements, directly targeting the physical infrastructure AI compute depends on.

The same ideas appear repeatedly in paired House and Senate bills. Sales and use tax exemptions for data centers are targeted for repeal in at least four separate measures, while two bills would establish a new data center moratorium and require a Public Utility Commission report. Other proposals add environmental impact statements, public hearings before approval, and stricter water appropriation permits for large groundwater users.

These bills treat data centers as a load on water, power, and local approval processes rather than an economic asset. Repealing tax exemptions raises the cost of construction, a moratorium halts new capacity, and water permit changes slow siting. For AI, that means the buildings and power that compute requires would become harder to add in Minnesota, pushing expansion elsewhere or raising its price.

The record shows bill titles and filing dates, not outcomes. It does not say which measures passed, were amended, or died, nor how much data center capacity already exists in the state. The list also includes many unrelated bills on health, education, and public safety, so the volume of entries overstates how much of the legislature's attention went to AI infrastructure.
